title: Origins of metallurgy
summary: People hammered native copper in Anatolia from roughly 9000 BCE, but extracting metal from ore and alloying came around 5000 BCE. In Europe the oldest evidence is in the southeastern Balkans, with copper ore mining around 6200 BC, the earliest smelting around 5000 BC and a boom in the mid-fifth millennium. Similar early work appears in the Middle East. Copper metallurgy reached the Carpathian Basin and East Central Europe around 4300 BC.

as_recorded.value: earliest evidence for smelting around 5000 BC
